followup.answer_html:
You now have three things.

  1. A commit-ready GitHub project called triage-desk: a customer-support agent built on LangGraph that classifies incoming messages, looks up orders, answers policy questions with a model, and pauses for a human to approve any refund over $50. It has typed state with reducers, a SQLite checkpointer so paused or crashed conversations resume where they left off, retries with backoff, timeouts, an error-handler fallback to a person, and a test suite (about 30 cases) that runs without an API key. out/README.md is the README, meant to be committed at the repository root as-is. out/repo-files.md holds every other file (pyproject.toml, LICENSE, .gitignore, .env.example, all source and test files) under its exact path - copy each block into place. Setup and a first run take under an hour (create a venv, pip install -e ".[dev]", add an Anthropic key, run pytest -q, then triage-desk chat). Nothing in the repo has actually been run yet, so run the tests first and read the README's "if you learned LangGraph from an older tutorial" table before pushing.

  2. A study guide, out/langgraph-study-guide.md (delivered separately as a PDF), that walks through the carousel's own 14 topics in order, each with a short explanation, a verified current-code snippet, and an explicit note wherever the carousel's own code is wrong. It also answers the deck's four open questions from the official docs, adds the three topics the deck's table of contents promised but never covered, and closes with a one-week, day-by-day reading-and-building path. Working through it at an hour or two a day takes about a week; on day 7 you end with a working, traced, persistent, tool-using agent as a base for a real project.

  3. A correction to the deck itself: the version numbers in the earlier research note (langgraph 1.2.12, langgraph-sdk 0.4.5, langgraph-checkpoint 4.2.0) were flagged as unverified - they have now been checked directly against PyPI and GitHub releases and are correct, and the repo is pinned to them.

One thing needs you directly: this repo and guide are built from a slide-by-slide read of the carousel, not from the creator's original 15-page PDF. If you want that PDF, comment "PDF" on the post yourself - the creator's automation replies to comments, and nothing else can trigger it on your behalf.

What the deck actually covers

The carousel's cover slide lists 15 subtopics ending with "13 Production Deployment," "14 Use Cases & Real-world Apps," and "15 Best Practices & Tips." None of those three exist in the deck - it ends at its own "Page 14," which is topic 9 on its own list (Debugging & Observability). The study guide fills that gap using the official deployment docs, so you're not missing anything by skipping the PDF for learning purposes - only for the creator's original wording and slide design.

# Build: triage-guard-agent

A resilient customer support triage agent with conditional tool execution, state persistence, and human-in-the-loop interrupt approval for refund actions.

I want a working repository I can push to GitHub. Build it completely -
runnable code, tests where they make sense, and a README.

## Why this matters
Goes beyond basic ReAct chatbot clones by implementing deterministic guardrail routing, checkpoint-backed state persistence, and explicit human-in-the-loop interrupts for sensitive transactions.

## Scope
Build these:
- TypedDict StateGraph
- arithmetic/order search tools
- SQLite checkpointer for session persistence
- conditional edge routing
- human-in-the-loop approval interrupt for actions over $50

Explicitly do NOT build these:
- Custom frontend UI
- multi-tenant authentication
- custom model fine-tuning

## Stack - use these exact versions
- Python 3.11+
- langgraph>=1.2.12
- langchain-core
- langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite
- langchain-anthropic or langchain-openai

## Milestones - each must be verifiably done before the next
1. **Define State and Reducers**
   - Done when: A TypedDict state schema with Annotated[list, operator.add] messages and metadata counters.
2. **Build Deterministic & Agentic Nodes**
   - Done when: LLM model node bound with search and calculation tools, plus a tool execution node.
3. **Add Conditional Routing & Persistence**
   - Done when: Conditional edges that route to tool nodes or terminate at END, compiled with an in-memory or SQLite checkpointer.
4. **Implement Human-in-the-Loop Interrupt**
   - Done when: The graph pauses execution using interrupt() whenever an order refund exceeds a set threshold, awaiting external review.

## README must cover
- Project Overview & Architecture Diagram (Mermaid graph)
- Key Engineering Concepts (Pregel cycles, Reducers, Durable State, Interrupts)
- Prerequisites and Environment Setup
- Step-by-Step Execution Guide (CLI simulation with human approval demo)
- Testing & Persistence Validation
- Future Roadmap

## Only after everything above works
- Migrate checkpointer backend from SQLite to PostgreSQL using langgraph-checkpoint-postgres.
- Add subgraphs for modular routing between billing and technical diagnostics.
- Attach LangSmith tracing to monitor execution super-steps and evaluate latency.

## Background
LangGraph is a low-level orchestration runtime and framework for building stateful, multi-actor LLM applications using graph architectures. Inspired by Google's Pregel system, it coordinates agents and deterministic code as nodes connected by edges, executing in discrete super-steps with explicit message-passing. It provides native persistence, cyclical execution loops, and first-class human-in-the-loop controls without abstracting away model prompts or code.

## Known traps - handle these, do not rediscover them
- State overwriting: Failing to use channel reducers like Annotated[list[AnyMessage], operator.add] causes nodes to overwrite the message history instead of appending to it.
- Missing compilation: Forgetting to call .compile() on the StateGraph builder before attempting to invoke or stream executions.
- Infinite loops in conditional edges: Not configuring a clean base case or terminal condition routing to END in conditional routing functions.
- Confusing the Graph API with the Functional API: LangGraph supports both StateGraph (Graph API) and function-based workflows (Functional API); mixing mental models can cause state synchronization bugs.

## How I want it delivered
- A single repository, ready to `git init` and push.
- Pin every dependency to the versions above.
- Tests that actually run. Python tests are run with pytest before
  any of this is published, and a failure stops the whole thing.
- A README that explains what it does and how to run it, written plainly.
- No placeholder code and no TODO stubs - if something is out of scope,
  leave it out rather than stubbing it.

## How to write it

Write the way I write. A graduate student saying plainly what
something does. First person where it is natural. Short sentences. No selling.

Plain ASCII punctuation only. No em dashes, en dashes, arrows, middots, curly
quotes, bullet characters, ellipsis characters, check marks or emoji. Hyphens
and straight quotes are fine.

Never say or imply that any AI tool, model or assistant had a hand in this.
No co-author lines, no credit, no mention of one anywhere. Naming a library
the project genuinely depends on is fine.

Do not use any of these words or phrases: seamless, seamlessly, elevate, unlock, leverage, dive into, deep dive, delve, a testament to, in the realm of, it is important to note, worth noting that, furthermore, moreover, cutting edge, cutting-edge, state of the art, state-of-the-art, game changer, game-changer, best in class, best-in-class, empower, streamline, plethora, myriad, revolutionize, harness the, boasts, in today's, ever-evolving, at its core, robust and scalable, first-class, battle-tested, rock-solid, supercharge, effortlessly, in conclusion, let's explore, we'll explore, whether you're, look no further, the world of.
Do not write "not just X but Y", or "it is not X, it is Y", or "more than just".

Comments explain why something is the way it is, not what the line does. No
comment blocks five lines long, no banner headers, no restating the function
name in a docstring. If a comment would only repeat the code, leave it out.

No padding, no marketing, and no section that exists only so there is a
section.
